slot.brief: Compute ΔH of a gaseous reaction using given bond enthalpies; moderate bookkeeping of bonds broken/formed.

verdicts.working: Bonds broken: 2(436) + 498 = 1370 kJ. Bonds formed: 4(463) = 1852 kJ. Thus ΔH = 1370 − 1852 = −482 kJ.

working:
Bonds broken: 2 H–H + 1 O=O → energy required = 2×436 + 498 = 1370 kJ.
Bonds formed: 4 O–H (2 H₂O) → energy released = 4×463 = 1852 kJ.
ΔH = (energy of bonds broken) − (energy of bonds formed) = 1370 − 1852 = −482 kJ.

Independent check: Bonds broken: 2(436) + 498 = 1370 kJ. Bonds formed: 4(463) = 1852 kJ. Thus ΔH = 1370 − 1852 = −482 kJ.
solution:
Bond enthalpy method: $\Delta H=\sum E(\text{bonds broken})-\sum E(\text{bonds formed})$.
$$\Delta H=[2(436)+498]-[4(463)]=1370-1852=-482\ \text{kJ}$$
